artboards.title: Alternative A: capture, backlog and list on one screen
Alternative B: editor with a metadata rail

annotations.text: As built (September 2026). Five screens at 1440×900. Fixed viewport: only inner panes scroll. Math and structures are approximated in these mockups; the app renders them with KaTeX, typst and smiles-drawer.

Alternative A: one home screen.
Capture, the review summary, and the filterable list live together; the to-define backlog becomes a filter chip instead of its own panel.
For: one place to add and find things, the list gets the whole height.
Against: no recently-added panel; capture and search compete for attention at the top.

Alternative B: metadata as a side rail.
Fields stack in a 280 px rail; editor and preview get the full height.
For: more vertical room, metadata always in view, chips wrap less awkwardly.
Against: editor and preview lose width; three columns get cramped below ~1300 px.
